items.text: What do emergency and ward staff at higher- and lower-performing hospitals describe as the barriers and facilitators to giving antibiotics within one hour to adults with suspected sepsis, by day and at night?
items.population: Emergency and ward staff involved in sepsis care at five hospitals
items.intervention: Delivery of the sepsis bundle, especially antibiotics within one hour (phenomenon of interest)
items.comparator: Higher- and lower-performing sites selected from network figures
items.outcome: Barriers and facilitators as described and observed
items.setting: Five hospitals in one regional network

finer: Feasible with one research nurse two days a week over four months; interesting to all five sepsis leads; novel in comparing sites and night care; ethical with staff consent; relevant because strategies cannot be chosen without it.
summary: One SPIDER question comparing higher- and lower-performing sites by day and night.
